source.title: Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms, II
source.authors: James Newton and Jack A. Thorne
readSections: The published version, read in full: the open-access (CC BY 4.0) PDF from pmihes.centre-mersenne.org/item/10.1007/s10240-021-00126-4.pdf (36 pages; SHA-256 ab39986290418f835708ca5f1114b231c628ef1efe5aa7f479f2666db6ae7a1b; fetched 23 September 2026; received 17 July 2020, revised 22 September 2021, accepted 25 September 2021, online 11 October 2021). summary: The paper completes Newton–Thorne I. For every non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) and every n, it proves that Sym^n π exists (Theorem A). Consequently every non-CM elliptic curve over ℚ has entire symmetric power L-functions (Corollary B). Appendix A adds the weight-one and CM cases. The proof inducts on the number of supercuspidal primes, starting from Newton–Thorne I Theorem B, by killing ramification in the manner of Khare–Wintenberger. Two things make the induction work. The first is a variant of good-dihedral primes: the 'seasoned' representations, with an extra Steinberg prime (Definition 3.6), which guarantee large residual image at each supercuspidal prime. The second is a new automorphy lifting theorem for symmetric powers (Theorem 2.1). It patches the rank-2 quaternionic deformation ring R together with the pseudodeformation ring P of Sym^{n−1}, where P is regular at the automorphic point by the vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups. This replaces any control of the dual Selmer group of Sym^{n−1} and works for residually reducible Sym^{n−1}, including p = 2. The endpoints are planned in ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 (ML.1/ML.5 for Appendix A). The method goes to one new Part II of that roadmap, beside the two proposed for Newton–Thorne I. The GL_2 inputs are planned in the Serre-conjecture, GL_2-lifting and local deformation roadmaps. After review, the extraction has 61 items: 1 library, 30 planned and 30 missing. The Newton–Thorne 2020 ring P and the adjoint Selmer vanishing, BLGGT14's lifting theorem, the relation ∼ and potential diagonalisability go to the polarized-lifting candidate. The Ribet–Momose large-image theorem and Gee's reduction theorem are sources of R19.3 and R07.4–R07.5. Four mistakes are recorded: two misprints (E1, E2), a gap in the case 2 ∈ sc(π) of the proof of Theorem 3.1 (E3), and a group of notational slips in §2 (E4). None affects a stated result.

items.name: Theorem A (Theorem 3.1): symmetric powers of every non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal form
items.statement: Let π be a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) which is non-CM. Then for each integer n ≥ 1, Sym^n π exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{n+1}(𝔸_ℚ) (Theorem 3.1: for n ≥ 1, Sym^{n−1}π exists).
items.locator: §1, Theorem A, p. 117; §3, Theorem 3.1, p. 139 (proof pp. 147–148)
items.note: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.3 plans Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy as an endpoint. The proof (killing supercuspidal primes with the new automorphy lifting Theorem 2.1) is routed to the Part II below; the case with no supercuspidal prime is PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 Theorem B.

items.name: Corollary B: analytic continuation of symmetric power L-functions of non-CM elliptic curves
items.statement: Let E/ℚ be an elliptic curve without complex multiplication. For each n ≥ 2 the completed symmetric power L-function Λ(Sym^n E, s) (as defined e.g. by Dummigan–Martin–Watkins) admits an analytic continuation to the entire complex plane.
items.note: From Theorem A and the modularity of elliptic curves over ℚ (Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor); ML.3 plans these analytic consequences.

items.name: Theorem A.1: symmetric powers of weight-one and CM forms
items.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) with π_∞ a holomorphic limit of discrete series, or the automorphic induction of a Hecke character of a quadratic field. Then Sym^n π exists (usually not cuspidal).
items.note: Proof: the Deligne–Serre representation has dihedral, A_4, S_4 or A_5 projective image; the dihedral and CM cases are isobaric sums of Hecke characters and automorphic inductions; A_4 needs Sym², S_4 needs Sym^m for m ≤ 3, and A_5 needs Sym^m for m ≤ 4 with the tensor products GL_2 × GL_2 → GL_4 and GL_2 × GL_3 → GL_6 (Kim 2004 Theorem 6.4), via the character tables of the binary polyhedral groups. Weight-one Deligne–Serre representations are ML.1; known symmetric-power and tensor transfers are registered in ML.5. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1 ('Construct the weight-one Artin representation in the Deligne–Serre setting') was added to the planned layers. The transfers used are item 46.

items.name: The setting of §2
items.statement: Let p be a prime, F a totally real field, ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ and n ≥ 1. π is a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight 2, non-CM, with r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} not ordinary (Thorne 2016 §5.1; hence potentially Barsotti–Tate) at every v | p, and such that for some a ≥ 1 with p^a > max(5, 2n − 1) there is a sandwich PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) ⊂ Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) ⊂ PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) up to conjugacy (so that Taylor–Wiles primes can be chosen with Sym^{n−1}r̄(Frob) regular semisimple).

items.name: Theorem 2.1: automorphy lifting for symmetric power representations
items.statement: In the setting of §2, suppose there is another regular algebraic cuspidal π′ of GL_2(𝔸_F) such that (1) π′ has weight 2 and is non-CM; (2) r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} is not ordinary for v | p; (3) r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}; (4) for each place v ∤ p, π_v is a character twist of Steinberg iff π′_v is; (5) Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} is automorphic. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic.
items.note: A new kind of automorphy lifting theorem, tailored to functoriality: it needs no dual Selmer control for Sym^{n−1}. After soluble base change one may assume (6) [F : ℚ] even, (7) det r_{π,ι} = det r_{π′,ι} = ϵ^{−1}, (8) π, π′ unramified at p, (9) Iwahori-spherical away from p with an even number of ramified places, (10) r̄ trivial on S = S_p ∪ Σ, q_v ≡ 1 mod p and π_v, π′_v Steinberg on Σ, (11) an everywhere unramified CM quadratic K/F in which S splits; then one proves Sym^{n−1}r_{Π,ι} automorphic for Π = π_K and descends.

items.name: Kisin's local lifting rings for weight-two forms
items.statement: For v | p the smallest reduced 𝒪-torsion-free quotient R_v of the fixed-determinant (ϵ^{−1}) lifting ring R^□_v through which non-ordinary crystalline lifts with Hodge–Tate weights {0, 1} factor is a domain of dimension 4 + [F_v : ℚ_p] (Kisin, Modularity of 2-adic Barsotti–Tate representations, Corollary 2.3.13); for v ∈ Σ, the quotient for extensions of ϵ^{−1} by the trivial character is a domain of dimension 4 (Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, Corollary 2.6.7); at infinite places R^{−1,□}_{V_F} (Kisin, Modularity of 2-adic Barsotti–Tate representations, Proposition 2.5.6) is a domain of dimension 3; R^{loc} = ⊗̂R_v is an 𝒪-flat domain of dimension 1 + 3[F : ℚ] + 3|S| (Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, Lemma 3.4.12).
items.note: Barsotti–Tate components are R08.4, Steinberg conditions away from p R08.2; the real-place and dyadic modifications are in GL2ModularityLifting R22.6. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): the two 'Kisin 2009' citations were made unambiguous (the paper's [Kis09a] is the 2-adic Barsotti–Tate paper, [Kis09b] the Annals paper), and LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.5 ('Supply the real-place, local-at-2 and twisting calculations required by KW II and Kisin's 2-adic Barsotti–Tate theorem') was added for the rings at the infinite places.

items.name: The global deformation rings R_Q, R_Q^□ and their p = 2 variants
items.statement: For Q finite and disjoint from S: Def_Q (lifts r̃ of r̄ unramified outside S ∪ Q with det r̃ = ϵ^{−1} and local components in the R_v), represented by R_Q (R = R_∅), the framed version Def^□_Q represented by R^□_Q with R^{loc} → R^□_Q, and (for p = 2) Def′_Q, Def′^{□}_Q with the determinant condition only on S, represented by R′_Q, R′^{□}_Q.
items.note: Representability and universal representations are R04.2, local conditions and presentations R04.3. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.4 ('Treat p=2 diagonalizable twisting groups … in the form used by KW II') was added for the p = 2 variants Def′_Q, Def′^□_Q, whose determinant is fixed only on S.

items.name: The pseudodeformation ring P of the symmetric power determinant
items.statement: With t = det Sym^{n−1}(r|_{G_K}) and t′ = det Sym^{n−1}(r′|_{G_K}) (group determinants in Chenevier's sense) and t̄ their common reduction, P ∈ 𝒞_𝒪 is the quotient R_S of R^{[0,n−1]}_{t̄,S} of Newton–Thorne 2020 §2.19: it represents conjugate self-dual group determinants of G_{K,S} lifting t̄ with similitude character ϵ^{1−n} which are semistable with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, n − 1].
items.note: Imported from Newton–Thorne, Adjoint Selmer groups of automorphic Galois representations of unitary type. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): rerouted from the new symmetric-power Part II to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting, together with item 17. Both are Newton–Thorne 2020 results about polarized (conjugate self-dual) pseudodeformation rings, used again by Newton–Thorne I and by PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26, so they need one general owner rather than a symmetric-power one. The generic determinant carrier and pseudorepresentation deformation functor that P refines are planned in IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.0 and GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1 (items 50–51). What is missing is the conjugate self-dual quotient with similitude ϵ^{1−n} and the semistable, Hodge–Tate [0, n−1] condition (2.16.1) of NT20.

items.name: Lemma 2.2: symmetric powers of Barsotti–Tate lifts are semistable in the torsion sense
items.statement: Let A ∈ 𝒞_𝒪 be Artinian, v ∈ S_p and r̃ : G_{F_v} → GL_2(A) a lift of r̄ of determinant ϵ^{−1} through R_v. Then A^n, via Sym^{n−1}r̃, is isomorphic as ℤ_p[G_{F_v}]-module to a subquotient of a lattice in a crystalline representation with Hodge–Tate weights in [0, n − 1]. Consequently Sym^{n−1} of the universal deformation defines a morphism P → R.
items.note: Proof: the dual of A² is the generic fibre of a finite flat group scheme; Berthelot–Breen–Messing Théorème 3.1.1 gives a crystalline lattice with weights in [0, 1] of which it is a quotient.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles data for symmetric powers and the rings P_Q
items.statement: A Taylor–Wiles datum of level N is (Q, Q̃, (α_v, β_v)_{v∈Q}) with Q places split in K, q_v ≡ 1 mod p^N, v = ṽṽ^c fixed, and α_v, β_v eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_v) such that α_v^{n−1}, α_v^{n−2}β_v, …, β_v^{n−1} are distinct. R_Q → R gives R_Q ⊗_{𝒪[Δ_Q]} 𝒪 ≅ R, Δ_Q = ∏k(v)^×(p). P_Q is the quotient of R_{S∪Q} (Newton–Thorne 2020 §2.19) of pseudodeformations t̃ abelian at each ṽ (so t̃|_{G_{K_ṽ}} is the determinant of unique characters χ_{v,1} ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_{v,n} lifting ur_{α^{n−i}β^{i−1}}; Allen–Newton–Thorne Proposition 2.5) with χ_{v,i}|_I = χ_{v,m}^{n+1−2i}|_I (n = 2m) or χ_{v,m}^{(n+1−2i)/2}|_I (n = 2m + 1); the χ_{v,m} make P_Q an 𝒪[Δ_Q]-algebra and there is a universal P_Q → R_Q (𝒪[Δ_Q]-linear when n is even).
items.note: The distinctness condition is stronger than for two-dimensional lifting and is what the sandwich hypothesis makes possible.

items.name: Proposition 2.3: quaternionic Hecke modules with Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: Let D be the definite quaternion algebra ramified exactly at ∞ and Σ, H_D(U) the 𝒪-valued functions on D^×\(D ⊗ 𝔸^∞)^×/(𝔸^∞)^×U, U_0 and U_1(Q; N) ⊂ U_0(Q) (Iwahori at Q with quotient Δ_Q/(p^N)), and m_D (with T^{(1)}_v ∈ m_D and T^{(2)}_v − 1 ∈ m_D at p), m_{D,Q}. For a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N + m_D: (1) m_D, m_{D,Q} are in the supports of H_D(U_0), H_D(U_0(Q)); (2) H_D(U_1(Q; N))_{m_{D,Q}} is free over 𝒪[Δ_Q/(p^N)] with coinvariants H_D(U_0)_{m_D}; (3) it is an R_Q-module with tr r_Q^{univ}(Frob_v) = T^{(1)}_v, det = q_vT^{(2)}_v, compatibly with the Δ_Q-actions.
items.note: Khare–Wintenberger II Corollary 7.5 and Lemma 9.1, Kisin Lemma 3.2.7, Jacquet–Langlands (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3). Auxiliary levels and freeness are GL2ModularityLifting R22.2.

items.name: Definite unitary Hecke modules with twisted Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: For the definite unitary group G over F split by K (Newton–Thorne 2020 §4.1): H_G(V) = functions G(F)\G(𝔸^∞_F)/V → 𝒪; V_0 (Iwahori at Σ); for a Taylor–Wiles datum V_1(Q; N)_v = ι_ṽ^{−1}{(a_ij) ∈ Iw_ṽ : ∏_i a_ii^{n+1−2i} ↦ 1 ∈ k(ṽ)^×(p)/(p^N)} (n even) or with exponents (n + 1 − 2i)/2 (n odd), so V_0(Q)/V_1(Q; N) ≅ Δ_Q/(p^N); Hecke operators ι^{−1}T^{(i)}_w and ι^{−1}U^{(i)}_{ϖ_ṽ}; m_G (characteristic polynomial of Sym^{n−1}r̄(Frob_w) = Σ(−1)^i q_w^{i(i−1)/2}T^{(i)}_wX^{n−i}) and m_{G,Q} (U^{(i)} − q^{i(1−i)/2}∏_{j≤i}α^{n−j}β^{j−1}); twisting by characters θ of U_1 through det.

items.name: Lemma 2.4: quadratic twists on the unitary side for p = 2
items.statement: Let n be even and p = 2, and χ : F^×\(𝔸^∞_F)^×/det U_1(Q; N) → 𝒪^× quadratic. There is a unique character θ_χ of U_1(F)\U_1(𝔸^∞_F)/det V_1(Q; N) with θ_χ(z/z^c) = χ(zz^c) for all z ∈ (𝔸^∞_K)^×.
items.note: Hilbert 90 for 0 → 𝔾_m → Res_{K/F}𝔾_m → U_1 → 0.

items.name: Proposition 2.5: unitary Hecke modules with Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: For a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N + m_G: (1) m_G, m_{G,Q} are in the supports of H_G(V_0), H_G(V_0(Q)); (2) H_G(V_1(Q; N))_{m_{G,Q}} is free over 𝒪[Δ_Q/(p^N)] with coinvariants H_G(V_0)_{m_G}; (3) it is a P_Q-module on which Λ^{univ}_i(Frob_w) (the coefficients of the universal characteristic polynomial, Chenevier §1.10) acts as q_w^{i(i−1)/2}T^{(i)}_w, compatibly with the Δ_Q-actions.
items.note: Proof: Labesse Théorème 5.4 and the existence of Π′_n (as in Newton–Thorne 2020 §4.3); via Δ′_Q, V′_1(Q; N) and P′_Q with the free action (Khare–Wintenberger II Lemma 7.4, Böckle–Harris–Khare–Thorne Lemma 8.18), Newton–Thorne 2020 Proposition 3.1 and Lemma 4.7, and Allen–Newton–Thorne Proposition 2.5 (uniqueness of the decomposition of multiplicity-free pseudocharacters). Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): the published proof (p. 130) cites [ANT20, Proposition 2.5] for the uniqueness of the decomposition of residually multiplicity-free pseudocharacters, where arXiv v2 cites [BC09, Proposition 1.5.1]; that input is item 51, and Labesse's Théorème 5.4 is item 49.

items.name: Proposition 2.6: patched rings and modules (p > 2)
items.statement: There is q ≥ 0 such that, with W_∞ = 𝒪[[Y_1, …, Y_q, Z_1, …, Z_{4|S∪S_∞|−1}]], there are complete Noetherian local W_∞-algebras P_∞, R_∞ with P_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ P and R_∞ ⊗ 𝒪 ≅ R, a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R_∞ with g = q + |S ∪ S_∞| − 1, a P_∞-module H_{G,∞} and an R_∞-module H_{D,∞}, both finite free over W_∞ and specialising to H_G = H_G(V_0)_{m_G} and H_D = H_D(U_0)_{m_D}, and a morphism P_∞ → R_∞ compatible with P → R.
items.note: Proof: Taylor–Wiles data from Lemma 2.7, the framing ring 𝒯, Newton–Thorne 2020 Lemma 2.16 (P_N a quotient of 𝒪[[X_1, …, X_{g_0}]]) and the diagonalisation of Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, Proposition 3.3.1. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): 'Kisin 2009' made unambiguous. The patching itself is item 19. The commutative algebra of the conclusion is item 52.

items.name: The support argument: regularity of P_∞ transfers automorphy
items.statement: Given Proposition 2.6 (or 2.8), H_{G,∞} and H_{D,∞} are Cohen–Macaulay with every component of support of dimension q + 4|S ∪ S_∞| (Stacks 0BUS), so R^{loc}[[X]] → R_∞ is an isomorphism, R_∞ is a domain and H_{D,∞} is faithful; since P_(p′) = E at the point p′ of t′ (vanishing of the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group of r_{Π′_n,ι}), P_∞ is regular of dimension q + 4|S ∪ S_∞| − 1 at p′_∞, so a unique component of Spec P_∞ through p′_∞ lies in Supp H_{G,∞}; the irreducible Spec R_∞ maps into it, hence p (the point of t) is in Supp_P H_G, which gives a RACSDC Π_n with r_{Π_n,ι} ≅ Sym^{n−1}(r|_{G_K}) (Labesse Corollaire 5.3), and descent (BLGHT11 Lemma 1.5).
items.note: The key new idea: a priori regularity of the pseudodeformation ring replaces killing the dual Selmer group of Sym^{n−1}.

items.name: Vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups: regularity of P at t′ (Newton–Thorne 2020)
items.statement: P_(p′) equals its residue field E, where p′ is the kernel of P → 𝒪 given by t′ (Newton–Thorne 2020 Theorem A, Proposition 2.21, Example 2.34: the adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer group of r_{Π′_n,ι} vanishes).
items.note: Imported from Newton–Thorne, J. Eur. Math. Soc. 25 (2023). Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): rerouted to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting with item 8; see the note there. PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 (item 73, routed to SymmetricPowersByAnalyticContinuation) and PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 (nt23-adjoint-selmer-vanishing, routed as a source of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions) place the same theorem elsewhere. Their reviews should move it to the same single owner.

items.name: Lemma 2.7: enough Taylor–Wiles data (p > 2)
items.statement: Let q = dim_k H¹(F_S/F, ad⁰r̄(1)) and g = q + |S ∪ S_∞| − 1. For every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N with a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R^□_Q of R^{loc}-algebras.
items.note: As Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorem 2.49 (Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, Proposition 3.2.5, Thorne 2016 Proposition 5.10), using H¹(PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), ad⁰) = 0 (Cline–Parshall–Scott Table 4.5) and σ with (α/β)^i ≠ 1 for i < n. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): the H¹-vanishing input is item 53, and the choice of primes uses the Chebotarev density theorem (item 54).

items.name: Taylor–Wiles–Kisin patching
items.statement: The abstract patching construction: from compatible systems of finite-level rings and modules with bounded cardinalities, pass by the pigeonhole principle to a subsequence and inverse limits R_∞, P_∞, H_{D,∞}, H_{G,∞} (Kisin 2009 Proposition 3.3.1).
items.note: Patching modules are DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5 and their arithmetic application GL2ModularityLifting R22.3.

items.name: Proposition 2.8: patched rings and modules (p = 2)
items.statement: There is q ≥ |S ∪ S_∞| − 2 such that, with W_∞ as before and γ = 2 − |S ∪ S_∞| + q, there are data (1)–(4) as in Proposition 2.6 but with R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R′_∞ → R_∞ (g = 2q + 1), (5) a free action of Ĝ_m^γ on Sp_{R′_∞} and an equivariant δ : Sp_{R′_∞} → Ĝ_m^γ (Ĝ_m^γ acting on itself by the square of the identity), with (6) δ^{−1}(1) = Sp_{R_∞} and the action of Ĝ_m^γ[2](𝒪) on R_∞ lifting to H_{D,∞}, and (7) an action of Ĝ_m^γ[2] on Sp_{P_∞} making Sp_{R_∞} → Sp_{P_∞} equivariant and lifting to H_{G,∞}.
items.note: The 2-adic patching of Khare–Wintenberger II §2 and Kisin; deduction via the invariant ring R^{inv}_∞ (KW II Proposition 2.5) and the transitivity of Ĝ_m^γ[2](𝒪) on components of Spec R_∞.

items.name: Lemma 2.9: enough Taylor–Wiles data (p = 2)
items.statement: Let q = dim_k H¹(F_S/F, ad r̄) − 2 and g = 2q + 1. Then q ≥ |S ∪ S_∞| − 2 and for every N ≥ 1 there is a Taylor–Wiles datum of level N with |Q| = q, a surjection R^{loc}[[X_1, …, X_g]] → R′^{□}_Q, and Θ_Q/(2^N) ≅ (ℤ/2^N)^γ, γ = 2 − |S ∪ S_∞| + q, for Θ_Q the Galois group of the maximal abelian pro-2 extension of F unramified outside Q and (S ∪ S_∞)-split.
items.note: Khare–Wintenberger II Lemma 5.10 with the stronger distinctness condition.

items.name: Definition 3.2: the semisimple conductor, and sc(π)
items.statement: For π regular algebraic cuspidal on GL_2(𝔸_ℚ), sc(π) is the set of primes p with π_p supercuspidal and M_π = ∏_l N((rec_{ℚ_l}π_l)^{ss}) is its semisimple conductor.

items.name: Lemma 3.3: conductors of reducible or dihedral residual representations
items.statement: If p is odd and r̄_{π,ι} is reducible or dihedral (induced from an index-two subgroup of G_ℚ), the prime-to-p part of its conductor divides M_π.

items.name: Lemma 3.4: a non-ordinary weight-two congruence with controlled type at p
items.statement: If Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) contains a conjugate of PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with p^a > 5, there is π′ regular algebraic cuspidal with (1) r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}; (2) π′ of weight 2 and not ι-ordinary; (3) rec π′_p ≅ ω_1 ⊕ ω_2 with ω_i of conductor dividing p³; (4) for l ≠ p, π_l is a Steinberg twist (resp. supercuspidal) iff π′_l is.
items.note: Proof: types M_l for the supercuspidal components (Breuil–Mézard Definition A.1.4.1), a quaternion algebra ramified at the Steinberg primes, a neat level from an auxiliary l_0, Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis Corollary 2.12, and a dimension count on the slope-(0, 1) part of H^δ(Y(U_0(p³)), M(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2)^∨) via Hida theory and Mackey's formula (Ind^{U_0(p)}_{U_0(p³)} contains χ_1ψ ⊗ χ_2ψ^{−1} with multiplicity p + 2 or p + 1); Geraghty Lemma 5.2 for non-ordinarity.

items.name: Lemma 3.5: adding a strong local connection away from p
items.statement: If p ≥ 3 and Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) ⊇ PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) with p^a > 5, there is π′ with (1) r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}; (2) weight 2, not ι-ordinary; (3) rec π′_p ≅ ω_1 ⊕ ω_2 of conductors dividing p³ (so N(π′_p) | p⁶); (4) r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} ∼ r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} for every l ≠ p, in particular N(π_l) = N(π′_l).
items.note: Lemma 3.4 with Gee's lifts of prescribed type (Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7) and BLGGT14 §1.3 ('strongly connect', Remark (6) on p. 524).

items.name: Definition 3.6: seasoned automorphic representations
items.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2 with 2 ∉ sc(π), and q, t, r primes. π is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) if (1) t | q + 1, t ∉ sc(π), t > max(10, 8n(n − 1)) and (q + 1)/t > 2; (2) rec π_q ≅ Ind^{W_{ℚ_q}}_{W_{ℚ_{q²}}}χ with χ|_{I_{ℚ_q}} of order t (so q ∈ sc(π), N(π_q) = q²); (3) r is a primitive root mod q and r ≡ 1 mod M, M the lcm of the prime-to-q part of M_π and ∏_{p∈sc(π)−{q}}p⁶; (4) π_r is an unramified twist of Steinberg; (5) for each p ∈ sc(π) and each irreducible dihedral ρ : G_ℚ → GL_2(𝔽̄_p) of prime-to-p conductor dividing Mq², there is a prime s with π_s an unramified Steinberg twist, ρ(Frob_s) scalar and s ≢ 1 mod p.
items.note: A variant of Khare–Wintenberger's good-dihedral condition, with an extra Steinberg prime r guaranteeing large image.

items.name: Proposition 3.7: seasoned representations have large residual image at supercuspidal primes
items.statement: If π is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r), then for each p ∈ sc(π) there is ι : Q̄_p ≅ ℂ with r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) containing a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) for some p^a > 2n − 1.
items.note: Proof: for p = q, irreducibility from the Steinberg prime r and Gee 2011 Theorem 4.6.1 (niveau-2 description), non-dihedrality from (5) and Lemma 3.3, and a choice of ι making the projective image contain an element of order ≥ t/2 > 4n(n − 1); for p ≠ q, inertia at q has projective order t; then the classification of finite subgroups of PGL_2(𝔽̄_p).

items.name: Lemma 3.8: the Galois group of a compositum is a fibre product
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension E/K with Galois subextensions K_1, K_2, the natural map Gal(K_1K_2/K) → Gal(K_1/K) ×_{Gal(K_1∩K_2/K)} Gal(K_2/K) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Mathlib's IntermediateField.restrictNormalHomSupProd is the injective joint restriction map; Tau Ceti identifies its range with the fibre product (IntermediateField.mem_range_restrictNormalHomSupProd_iff, TauCeti/FieldTheory/Galois/FiberProduct.lean).

items.name: Proposition 3.9: making a representation seasoned
items.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2, non-CM, with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π). There is π′ regular algebraic cuspidal with (1) primes (q, t, r) such that π′ is seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) and sc(π′) = sc(π) ∪ {q}; (2) Sym^{n−1}π′ exists iff Sym^{n−1}π does.
items.note: Proof: t > max(10, 8n(n − 1), N(π)) with t ≡ 1 mod 4 and large t-adic image, q ≡ −1 mod t with Frob_q conjugate to complex conjugation, r and the primes s_{i,j} by Chebotarev with Lemma 3.8, then Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7 and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 (Fontaine–Laffaille at t; Sym^m of SL_2(𝔽_t) irreducible for t > m).

items.name: Proposition 3.10: removing one supercuspidal prime
items.statement: Let π be regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2, seasoned with respect to (q, t, r), and p ∈ sc(π) with p ≥ 5. There is π′ of weight 2, non-CM, with sc(π′) = sc(π) − {p}, still seasoned with respect to (q, t, r) if p ≠ q, such that Sym^{n−1}π′ existing implies Sym^{n−1}π exists.
items.note: Proposition 3.7 chooses ι, Lemma 3.5 produces π′ and Theorem 2.1 transfers automorphy.

items.name: Proposition 3.11: the weight-two case with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π)
items.statement: If π is regular algebraic cuspidal of weight 2, non-CM, with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π), then Sym^{n−1}π exists.
items.note: Induction: (H_k) ⇒ (H′_{k+1}) by Proposition 3.10 and (H′_k) ⇒ (H_k) by Propositions 3.9–3.10; (H_0) is Newton–Thorne I.

items.name: The reductions in the proof of Theorem 3.1
items.statement: For π of weight 2 with 2 ∉ sc(π) and π_3 supercuspidal: choose t > max(5, 4n(n − 1), N(π)), t ≡ 1 mod 4, with Proj r̄_{π,ι_t}(G_ℚ) conjugate to PSL_2(𝔽_t) or PGL_2(𝔽_t) (item 56), and q ≡ −1 mod t, q ≡ 1 mod 8, q ≡ 1 mod every prime l < t, with Frob_q conjugate to complex conjugation (Chebotarev); a good-dihedral π′ at q (Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7) with Sym^{n−1}π′ existing iff Sym^{n−1}π does (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1); the 3-adic projective image of r̄_{π′,ι} is PSL_2(𝔽_{3^a}) or PGL_2(𝔽_{3^a}) with 3^a > 2n − 1 (Khare–Wintenberger I Lemma 6.3); Lemma 3.4 gives a weight-2 π″ with r̄_{π″,ι} ≅ r̄_{π′,ι}, 2, 3 ∉ sc(π″), r_{π″,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_3}} potentially crystalline and non-ordinary, and the same Steinberg primes away from 3; Proposition 3.11 and Theorem 2.1 conclude. The case 2 ∈ sc(π) runs the same argument with 3 replaced by 2 and concludes by the case just treated: π″ then has weight 2 and 2 ∉ sc(π″), but it may have 3 ∈ sc(π″), so Proposition 3.11 does not apply to it directly (sourceIssues E3). Weight k > 2 reduces to weight 2 through a t-adic congruence (t > max(5, k(n + 1)), π_t unramified, image of r̄_{π,ι} containing SL_2(𝔽_t)) with a weight-2, potentially crystalline π′ from Lemma 3.4, and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 with potential diagonalisability (Gee–Kisin Lemma 4.4.1 and the remark after BLGG11 Definition 3.3.5).
items.note: Printed with r̄_{π,ι} where r̄_{π′,ι} is meant in the 3-adic image step (sourceIssues E1). Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): statement corrected against pp. 147–148. The published text says 'potentially crystalline' (arXiv v2: 'potentially Barsotti–Tate'). The 2 ∈ sc(π) case must end with the case already treated rather than with Proposition 3.11 (E3). The large-image choice of t (item 56) is now explicit.

items.name: Good-dihedral primes and residual image control (Khare–Wintenberger)
items.statement: A form with a supercuspidal component at a good-dihedral prime q (inertia character of order t, t ≡ 1 mod 4, q ≡ 1 mod 8 and q ≡ 1 mod the primes below t) has large residual projective image at the relevant primes (Khare–Wintenberger I Lemmas 6.3 and 8.2).
items.note: Good-dihedral primes and their image control are ClassicalSerreModularity R27.1 and R33.2.

items.name: Automorphic lifts of prescribed type for GL_2 (Gee 2011)
items.statement: Gee 2011 Corollary 3.1.7 (with Proposition 3.1.5): given a modular r̄ with suitably large image, there is a weight-2 regular algebraic cuspidal π′ with r̄_{π′} ≅ r̄ with prescribed local behaviour — unramified Steinberg twists at chosen primes, a supercuspidal type at q, and r_{π,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} ∼ r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{ℚ_l}} elsewhere.
items.note: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.3 plans the prescribed local lifts, including 'any prescribed-type strengthening from Gee/Snowden used by the modern route'. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): Theorem 4.6.1 of Gee 2011, a local statement about reductions of potentially Barsotti–Tate representations of tame type that R24.3 does not plan, was split off as item 61.

items.name: Types for supercuspidal Bernstein components of GL_2(ℚ_l) (Henniart's appendix to Breuil–Mézard)
items.statement: For π_l supercuspidal there is, after enlarging E, an 𝒪[GL_2(ℤ_l)]-module M_l, finite free over 𝒪, with M_l ⊗ ℂ a type for the Bernstein component of π_l (Breuil–Mézard Definition A.1.4.1); and for principal-series types χ_1 ⊗ χ_2 on U_0(p^r), rec π′_p ≅ ω_1 ⊕ ω_2 with ω_i ∘ Art|_{ℤ_p^×} = ιχ_i and Hom_{U_0(p³)}(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2, π′_p) one-dimensional (A.2.4).
items.note: Types for GL_2 belong with the types Part II proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21.

items.name: Automorphy lifting for residually irreducible symmetric powers (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1)
items.statement: (BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1.) Let F be an imaginary CM field, l an odd prime and (r, μ) a regular algebraic, irreducible, n-dimensional polarized representation of G_F. Let d be the maximal dimension of an irreducible subrepresentation of the restriction of r̄ to the closed subgroup of G_F generated by the Sylow pro-l subgroups. Suppose that r|_{G_{F_v}} is potentially diagonalisable for every v | l (item 59), that r̄|_{G_{F(ζ_l)}} is irreducible, l ≥ 2(d + 1) and ζ_l ∉ F, and that (r̄, μ̄) is ordinarily automorphic or potentially diagonalisably automorphic. Then (r, μ) is potentially diagonalisably automorphic. The paper applies it over ℚ (after base change to a CM field and soluble descent, item 48) to r = Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι_t}, with Sym^{n−1}r̄_{π,ι_t} ≅ Sym^{n−1}r̄_{π′,ι_t} irreducible because the image of r̄ contains SL_2(𝔽_t) with t > n − 1, t large compared with n, and potential diagonalisability from Fontaine–Laffaille theory at t or from Gee–Kisin Lemma 4.4.1 with the remark after BLGG11 Definition 3.3.5.
items.locator: §3, proofs of Proposition 3.9 and Theorem 3.1, pp. 145–148
items.note: The residually irreducible polarized lifting theorem is in the Part II proposed by PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25. Review (REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B): statement corrected: it omitted the hypotheses of BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1 (a CM base field, polarization, l ≥ 2(d + 1), ζ_l ∉ F and irreducibility of r̄ over F(ζ_l)), which were read in the BLGGT14 source. The paper's choices t > 8n(n − 1) (Proposition 3.9), t > 4n(n − 1) with n ≥ 3 (Theorem 3.1) and t > k(n + 1) satisfy them.

items.name: Quaternionic automorphic forms of given type and the Jacquet–Langlands correspondence
items.statement: For a quaternion algebra D over ℚ ramified at the Steinberg primes Σ (and at ∞ iff |Σ| is odd), the cohomology H^δ(Y(U), M(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2)^∨) of the locally symmetric space of level U (Newton–Thorne 2016 §3.1) localised at m_π is non-zero (Buzzard–Diamond–Jarvis Corollary 2.12), and its systems of eigenvalues come, by Jacquet–Langlands, from cuspidal π′ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) of weight 2 with prescribed Steinberg and supercuspidal types.
items.note: Global Jacquet–Langlands is GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3; quaternionic Galois representations AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.2.

items.name: The symmetric power lift Sym^n π
items.statement: Let F be a number field, π a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) and n ≥ 1. Sym^n π exists if there is an automorphic representation Sym^n π of GL_{n+1}(𝔸_F) such that for every place v of F the Langlands parameter of (Sym^n π)_v is the image of the Langlands parameter of π_v under Sym^n : GL_2 → GL_{n+1}, the n-th symmetric power of the standard representation.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. ML.5 registers 'selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers with exact hypotheses' and ML.0 the local parameters and normalisations. For regular algebraic π over ℚ the paper passes freely between 'Sym^n π exists' and 'Sym^n r_{π,ι} is automorphic' (Theorem 2.1 against Propositions 3.9–3.10). That passage is the local–global compatibility of item 40 together with strong multiplicity one.

items.name: Local Langlands for GL_n, its Tate normalisation, and Weil–Deligne representations
items.statement: For K a non-archimedean local field of characteristic 0: WD(ρ) = (r, N) is the Weil–Deligne representation of a continuous ρ : G_K → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) (de Rham when p is the residue characteristic) and WD(ρ)^{F-ss} its Frobenius semisimplification; Art_K : K^× → W_K^{ab} sends uniformisers to geometric Frobenius elements; rec_K is the local Langlands bijection between irreducible admissible ℂ[GL_n(K)]-modules and Frobenius-semisimple n-dimensional Weil–Deligne representations over ℂ; and rec^T_K(π) = rec_K(π ⊗ |·|^{(1−n)/2}) is its Tate normalisation (Clozel–Thorne 2014, §2.1).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. ET.6 constructs the correspondence with full Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameters, R16.3 its GL_2 specialisation, and R01.2 Weil–Deligne representations.

items.name: Galois representations of regular algebraic polarizable cuspidal representations
items.statement: Let F be a CM or totally real field and π a cuspidal, regular algebraic, polarizable (in the sense of BLGGT14) automorphic representation of GL_n(𝔸_F). For every isomorphism ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ there is a continuous semisimple r_{π,ι} : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) with WD(r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}})^{F-ss} ≅ rec^T_{F_v}(ι^{−1}π_v) for every finite place v, including v | p (Caraiani 2014). For n = 2 and π of weight k, the Hodge–Tate weights of r_{π,ι} are {0, k − 1} (the cyclotomic character having weight −1) and ϵ^{k−1} det r_{π,ι} has finite order.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. AG2.2 constructs the polarized systems, AG2.5 proves the local–global comparison (including 'the Caraiani/Taylor–Yoshida upgrades') and AG2.6 the coefficient-prime comparison. R19.4–R19.5 are the rank-two Hilbert case. Planned in the same layers as PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 item 7.

items.name: Regular algebraic cuspidal representations of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) are twists of holomorphic eigenforms
items.statement: A cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) is regular algebraic exactly when it corresponds to a twist of a cuspidal Hecke eigenform f of some weight k ≥ 2 (Gelbart 1975, §3); π then has weight k in the sense of the Notation (W = (Sym^{k−2}ℂ²)^∨). Over a totally real field the cuspidal representations of weight k are those associated to cuspidal Hilbert modular forms of parallel weight k.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. R16.6: 'Identify the holomorphic representations over Q with the existing newforms, including level, character, weight, Hecke eigenvalues and normalisation. Define the Hilbert cohomological weights.' This is how the abstract's statement for eigenforms f follows from Theorem A.

items.name: Newton–Thorne I, Theorem B: symmetric powers without supercuspidal components
items.statement: Let π be a regular algebraic, non-CM, cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) such that π_p is not supercuspidal for any prime p. Then for every n ≥ 1, Sym^n π exists as a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_{n+1}(𝔸_ℚ).
items.locator: §1, pp. 117–118; §3, p. 139 and proof of Proposition 3.11, p. 146 (the hypothesis (H_0))
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. The base case |sc(π)| = 0 of the induction. It is PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 item 2, planned in ML.3 as an endpoint, with its proof routed to the Part IIs of that extraction.

items.name: Modularity of elliptic curves over ℚ (Breuil–Conrad–Diamond–Taylor)
items.statement: Every elliptic curve E over ℚ is modular: there is a weight-2 cuspidal automorphic representation π_E of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ), attached to a newform of level the conductor of E, with r_{π_E,ι} ≅ H¹_ét(E_{ℚ̄}, ℚ_p) ⊗ ℚ̄_p for every ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ; π_E is non-CM when E has no complex multiplication.
items.locator: §1, Corollary B and the sentence before it, p. 118
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. R29.6 states the unconditional modularity theorem 'with a weight-two rational newform of exact conductor' and transfers the analytic continuation of L(E, s).

items.name: Standard L-functions of cuspidal representations of GL_m are entire (Godement–Jacquet)
items.statement: For m ≥ 2 and a cuspidal automorphic representation Π of GL_m(𝔸_F), the completed standard L-function Λ(s, Π) extends to an entire function of s and satisfies Λ(s, Π) = ε(s, Π) Λ(1 − s, Π^∨).
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. Corollary B applies this to Π = Sym^n π_E (m = n + 1 ≥ 3), with π_E from item 43. The Euler factors of Λ(Sym^n E, s) (item 45) agree with those of Sym^n π_E up to the normalising shift at every prime, because (Sym^n π_E)_p has parameter Sym^n rec(π_{E,p}) (item 38) and rec(π_{E,p}) is the Weil–Deligne representation of E at p (item 40). AL.2 builds 'the adelic global integral for cuspidal GL_n representations, [with] … analytic continuation and functional equation with the n=1 exceptional pole separated'.

items.name: The completed symmetric power L-function Λ(Sym^n E, s)
items.statement: For an elliptic curve E over ℚ and n ≥ 1, Λ(Sym^n E, s) is the product of the archimedean Γ-factor of Sym^n H¹(E(ℂ), ℚ) and the Euler factors det(1 − Frob_p p^{−s} | (Sym^n H¹_ét(E_{ℚ̄}, ℚ_l))^{I_p})^{−1} (l ≠ p) over all primes p, as defined e.g. in Dummigan–Martin–Watkins 2009.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. The paper refers to DMW09 for the definition, and the review stated it as the standard motivic L-function. ML.3 owns 'the resulting analytic … arguments' of symmetric-power automorphy.

items.name: Low symmetric powers and tensor products for GL_2 (Gelbart–Jacquet, Kim–Shahidi, Kim, Ramakrishnan)
items.statement: For cuspidal π, π′ of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) and σ of GL_3(𝔸_ℚ): Sym^m π exists for m ≤ 4 (Gelbart–Jacquet for m = 2, Kim–Shahidi for m = 3, Kim for m = 4); the tensor products π ⊠ π′ on GL_4 (Ramakrishnan) and π ⊠ σ on GL_6 (Kim–Shahidi) exist; and for π of icosahedral weight one, Sym^n π exists for every n (Kim 2004, Theorem 6.4).
items.locator: §1, p. 118; Appendix A, proof of Theorem A.1, pp. 149–150
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. The paper cites only Kim 2004, Theorem 6.4, and 'Kim and Shahidi's results on tensor product and symmetric power functoriality'. The individual attributions are the standard ones and were supplied by the review. ML.5 registers 'selected tensor/symmetric-power transfers'.

items.name: Ordinary and non-ordinary weight-two representations at p
items.statement: For v | p, r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} is ordinary in the sense of Thorne 2016, §5.1, and π is ι-ordinary when this holds at every v | p. The paper uses three facts. (i) A weight-2 π with r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} not ordinary is potentially Barsotti–Tate at v. (ii) If π′ has weight 2 and ι^{−1}π′_p|_{U_0(p³)} contains χ_1 ⊗ χ_2, on which [U_0(p³)α_{p,1}U_0(p³)] acts by an eigenvalue of p-adic valuation strictly between 0 and 1, then π′ is not ι-ordinary (Geraghty 2019, Lemma 5.2). (iii) A supercuspidal π_p is never ι-ordinary.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. R19.5 proves the local statements at the coefficient prime, 'including the cases required for Barsotti–Tate, ordinary and endpoint-weight lifting'. R08.4 treats the finite-flat and Barsotti–Tate components 'separately in the ordinary and nonordinary cases'.

items.name: Soluble base change and descent
items.statement: (a) If F′/F is a soluble Galois extension of totally real fields and π is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) that is not automorphically induced from a quadratic subextension, the base change π_{F′} exists and is cuspidal, with r_{π_{F′},ι} ≅ r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F′}} (Langlands, Arthur–Clozel); in particular the soluble totally real extension of the preliminary reduction of Theorem 2.1 and the CM quadratic extension K/F with Π = π_K are available. (b) If F′/F is a soluble Galois extension of CM or totally real fields and r : G_F → GL_n(ℚ̄_p) is continuous with r|_{G_{F′}} irreducible and automorphic, then r is automorphic (BLGHT11, Lemma 1.5).
items.locator: §2, preliminary reduction and proof of Theorem 2.1, pp. 122–123 and 131
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. R17.4 proves cyclic and solvable base change and descent for GL_2. ML.5 registers cyclic base change for GL_n, as for PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 item 126. Statement (b) is given as the paper uses it.

items.name: Base change between definite unitary groups and GL_n (Labesse)
items.statement: For the definite unitary group G over F split by K/F of NT20 §4.1: (a) (Labesse 2011, Théorème 5.4) the RACSDC representation Π′_n of GL_n(𝔸_K) descends to G, so that m_G and m_{G,Q} lie in the supports of H_G(V_0) and H_G(V_0(Q)) (Proposition 2.5(1), argued as in NT20 §4.3); (b) (Labesse 2011, Corollaire 5.3) if the point 𝔭 of t lies in Supp_P H_G and Sym^{n−1}(r|_{G_K}) is irreducible, there is a RACSDC representation Π_n of GL_n(𝔸_K) with r_{Π_n,ι} ≅ Sym^{n−1}(r|_{G_K}).
items.locator: §2, proof of Proposition 2.5, p. 129; proof of Theorem 2.1, p. 131
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. ET.7a constructs 'the unitary-to-GL_m cohomological base-change character identities', and AG2.2 applies them. PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21 items 10–11 are planned in the same layers. Stated as the paper uses it.

items.name: Group determinants and the coefficients of their characteristic polynomial (Chenevier)
items.statement: An n-dimensional determinant of a group Γ with values in a commutative ring A is a multiplicative homogeneous polynomial law D : A[Γ] → A of degree n. Its characteristic polynomial is D(X − γ) = Σ_{i=0}^n (−1)^i Λ_i(γ) X^{n−i} with Λ_i : Γ → A (Chenevier 2014, §1.10). A representation ρ : Γ → GL_n(A) has the determinant det ∘ ρ. For Γ profinite and A ∈ 𝒞_𝒪 continuity is required, and t = det Sym^{n−1}(r|_{G_K}), t′ and their reduction t̄ are such determinants.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. IHG.0: 'Define a determinant as a multiplicative degree-n law D:A[G]→A with D(1)=1. Prove characteristic-polynomial identities, direct sum/product, duality…'.

items.name: Unique decomposition of residually multiplicity-free abelian determinants
items.statement: Let A ∈ 𝒞_𝒪, H a profinite group and D a continuous n-dimensional A-valued determinant of H that factors through H^{ab} and whose reduction is the determinant of χ̄_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ̄_n with pairwise distinct characters χ̄_i. Then there are unique characters χ_i : H → A^× lifting the χ̄_i with D = det(χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n) (Allen–Newton–Thorne 2020, Proposition 2.5, extending Bellaïche–Chenevier Proposition 1.5.1 to arbitrary characteristic; cf. NT20 Lemma 4.28).
items.locator: §2, definition of P_Q, p. 125; proof of Proposition 2.5, pp. 129–130
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. Applied to H = G_{K_ṽ} for v ∈ Q. IHG.1 constructs 'generalized matrix algebra decompositions under residually multiplicity-free hypotheses'. Stated as the paper uses it.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulay patched modules and components through a regular point
items.statement: (a) If W → R is a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings with W regular and M is a finite R-module that is finite free over W, then M is a Cohen–Macaulay R-module with dim Supp_R(M) = dim W. (b) If M is a finite Cohen–Macaulay module over a Noetherian local ring R, every associated prime 𝔭 of M is minimal in Supp(M) and dim R/𝔭 = dim Supp(M) (Stacks, Tag 0BUS). (c) If 𝔭 is a prime of a Noetherian local ring P with P_𝔭 regular, then 𝔭 lies on a unique irreducible component of Spec P. (d) If a Noetherian local domain surjects onto a ring carrying a finite module whose support has a component of the same dimension, the surjection is an isomorphism and the module is faithful.
items.locator: §2, proof of Theorem 2.1 for p > 2, p. 131, and for p = 2, pp. 136–137
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. The commutative algebra behind item 16. The review checked (b) against Stacks Lemma 10.103.7. R03.3 develops 'Cohen–Macaulay rings/modules … equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas', and R03.6 'when a patched module is faithful … or supported on a specified union of components'.

items.name: Vanishing of H¹(PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), ad⁰) (Cline–Parshall–Scott)
items.statement: For p odd and p^a > 5, H¹(PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), ad⁰) = 0, where ad⁰ is the trace-zero adjoint representation (Cline–Parshall–Scott 1975, Table (4.5)). Moreover, if Γ is PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) or PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}), then [Γ, Γ] ≅ PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) is non-abelian simple and acts absolutely irreducibly on ad⁰.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. R04.5 combines 'Chebotarev, residual-image lemmas and dual Selmer calculations' to choose Taylor–Wiles primes, and R01.4 owns the finite-subgroup facts of GL_2/PGL_2.

items.name: The Chebotarev density theorem
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension L/K of number fields and a conjugacy class C of Gal(L/K), the set of primes of K unramified in L whose Frobenius class is C has Dirichlet density #C/#Gal(L/K); in particular it is infinite.
items.locator: §2, proof of Lemma 2.7, p. 132; §3, proof of Proposition 3.9, p. 144, and of Theorem 3.1, p. 147
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. Tau Ceti f790474 has the Frobenius prime sets and their partition (NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet, TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/FrobeniusPrimeSet.lean) but not the density theorem. Its Chebotarev roadmap's Layer 10 plans it as hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet, with 'infinitude of every Frobenius class' derived. PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-26 plans the same item in AN.4.

items.name: Finite subgroups of PGL_2(𝔽̄_p) (Dickson)
items.statement: A finite subgroup H of PGL_2(𝔽̄_p) is conjugate to a subgroup of the image of the upper-triangular Borel subgroup, or is cyclic of order prime to p, or dihedral of order 2m with m prime to p, or isomorphic to A_4, S_4 or A_5, or conjugate to PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) or PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) for some a ≥ 1. Consequently, if the image of an irreducible, non-dihedral ρ̄ : G → GL_2(𝔽̄_p) has projective image containing an element of order prime to p and greater than 5, then up to conjugacy PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) ⊂ Proj ρ̄(G) ⊂ PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) for some a.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. R01.4: 'Prove the finite-subgroup facts of GL₂/PGL₂ used in the source arguments, including dihedral and exceptional images'. Planned there as in PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-25 (item 'dickson'). It is also used for the sandwich in Proposition 3.10 and in the proof of Theorem 3.1.

items.name: Large residual image for non-CM modular forms (Ribet, Momose)
items.statement: Let π be a non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ). For all but finitely many primes t that split completely in the coefficient field of π, and every isomorphism ι : ℚ̄_t → ℂ, the image of r̄_{π,ι} contains a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_t), so that Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) is conjugate to PSL_2(𝔽_t) or PGL_2(𝔽_t). In particular, such t exist with t ≡ 1 mod 4 and t larger than any given bound.
items.locator: §3, proof of Proposition 3.9, p. 144; proof of Theorem 3.1, pp. 147–148
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. The paper uses this without citation: 'Fix a prime t > max(10, 8n(n−1), N(π)) such that t ≡ 1 mod 4 and there exists an isomorphism ι … such that G = Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_ℚ) is conjugate either to PSL_2(𝔽_t) or PGL_2(𝔽_t)' (p. 144), and in the weight k > 2 case 'the image of r̄_{π,ι} contains a conjugate of SL_2(𝔽_t)' (p. 148). Sources: K. Ribet, 'On l-adic representations attached to modular forms II', Glasgow Math. J. 27 (1985); F. Momose, J. Fac. Sci. Univ. Tokyo 28 (1981). No layer plans it. R19.3 builds the compatible family of a fixed eigenform, R01.4 only the group theory of images, and the proposed open-image Part II of PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 covers Tate modules of abelian varieties, not modular forms of weight k > 2. Routed as a source of R19.3.

items.name: Hida's control theorem for the ordinary quaternionic cohomology of Lemma 3.4
items.statement: With D, the neat level U, the type coefficients M, δ ∈ {0, 1} and m_π as in Lemma 3.4, and characters χ_1, χ_2 : (ℤ/p³ℤ)^× → 𝒪^× lifting χ̄_1, χ̄_2 : 𝔽_p^× → k^×: dim_E H^δ(Y(U_0(p³)), M_E(χ_1 ⊗ χ_2)^∨)^{s=0}_{m_π} = dim_k H^δ(Y(U_0(p)), M_k(χ̄_1 ⊗ χ̄_2)^∨)^{ord}_{m_π}, where the superscripts denote the parts on which [U_0(p^r)α_{p,1}U_0(p^r)] acts by p-adic units.

Stated as the paper uses it.

items.name: Connecting and strongly connecting local Galois representations (BLGGT14 §1)
items.statement: For a finite extension K/ℚ_p and continuous ρ_1, ρ_2 : G_K → GL_n(𝒪_{ℚ̄_l}) (potentially crystalline when l = p), ρ_1 connects to ρ_2, written ρ_1 ∼ ρ_2, if ρ̄_1 ≅ ρ̄_2 and ρ_1, ρ_2 define points on a common irreducible component of Spec(R^□_{ρ̄_1} ⊗ ℚ̄_l) (for l = p, of the potentially crystalline lifting ring with the given Hodge–Tate weights). ρ_1 strongly connects to ρ_2, written ρ_1 ⇝ ρ_2, if moreover ρ_1 lies on a unique irreducible component. For l ≠ p, with WD(ρ_i) = (r_i, N_i): ρ_1 ∼ ρ_2 implies r_1|_{I_K} ≅ r_2|_{I_K}; ρ_1 ⇝ ρ_2 and ρ_2 ⇝ ρ_1 imply (r_1|_{I_K}, N_1) ≅ (r_2|_{I_K}, N_2), so the conductors agree (Remark (6) on p. 524); ρ_1 ∼ ρ_2 and H⁰(G_K, (ad ρ_1)(1)) = 0 imply ρ_1 ⇝ ρ_2; and ∼ is preserved by restriction to finite extensions, direct sums, tensor products and duals.
items.locator: Notation, p. 120; §3, proof of Lemma 3.5, p. 142; proofs of Propositions 3.9 and 3.10, pp. 145–146
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. Read in BLGGT14 §1.3 (l ≠ p) and §1.4 (l = p). In Lemma 3.5, 'by purity' supplies H⁰(G_{ℚ_l}, (ad ρ)(1)) = 0, hence strong connection in both directions and N(π_l) = N(π′_l). No layer plans the relation: LocalGaloisDeformationRings constructs the rings and their components (R08.2, L7), but not BLGGT's relation. Routed with the BLGGT14 lifting theorem (item 36) to PolarizedAutomorphyLifting.

items.name: Potentially diagonalisable representations (BLGGT14 §1.4)
items.statement: A continuous ρ : G_K → GL_n(𝒪_{ℚ̄_l}), with K/ℚ_l finite, is diagonalisable if it is crystalline and connects to a sum χ_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ χ_n of crystalline characters, and potentially diagonalisable if ρ|_{G_{K′}} is diagonalisable for some finite extension K′/K. This depends only on ρ ⊗ ℚ̄_l and is preserved by restriction to finite extensions. Potentially diagonalisable representations include: those with an invariant filtration with one-dimensional graded pieces, e.g. ordinary ones, and crystalline representations over an unramified K with every τ-Hodge–Tate multiset in an interval [a_τ, a_τ + l − 2] (Fontaine–Laffaille; BLGGT14 Lemma 1.4.3); two-dimensional potentially Barsotti–Tate representations (Gee–Kisin 2014, Lemma 4.4.1); and symmetric powers, tensor products and direct sums of potentially diagonalisable representations (the remark after BLGG11 Definition 3.3.5).
items.locator: §3, proof of Proposition 3.9, p. 146; proof of Theorem 3.1, pp. 147–148
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. The definition and Lemma 1.4.3 were read in BLGGT14; the other two inputs are stated as the paper uses them. Fontaine–Laffaille theory itself is planned in FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.3 and LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7. No layer plans potential diagonalisability. items.name: Free actions of Ĝ_m^γ and their invariant rings (Khare–Wintenberger II)
items.statement: Let A ∈ 𝒞_𝒪 with a free action of Ĝ_m^γ on Sp_A. The subring of invariants A^{inv} ⊂ A (KW II §2.4) satisfies: Sp_A → Sp_{A^{inv}} is smooth of relative dimension γ (KW II Proposition 2.5). If δ : Sp_A → Ĝ_m^γ is equivariant for the squaring action and B is the quotient with Sp_B = δ^{−1}(1), then Sp_B → Sp_{A^{inv}} is a torsor under Ĝ_m^γ[2].
items.locator: §2, proof of Theorem 2.1, case p = 2, p. 137
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. Used to show that R′_∞ ≅ R_loc⟦X_1, …, X_g⟧ and that Ĝ_m^γ[2](𝒪) permutes the components of Spec R_∞ transitively. R04.4 treats 'p=2 diagonalizable twisting groups … in the form used by KW II, including their stabilisers' and R22.6 'all twisting arguments'. Stated as the paper uses it.

items.name: Reductions of potentially Barsotti–Tate representations of tame supercuspidal type (Gee 2011, Theorem 4.6.1)
items.statement: Let ω_2 be the Teichmüller lift of a fundamental character of niveau 2 of I_{ℚ_q}, and ρ : G_{ℚ_q} → GL_2(ℚ̄_q) potentially Barsotti–Tate with inertial type ω_2^m ⊕ ω_2^{qm}, where m = i + (q + 1)j with i ∈ {1, …, q}. If ρ̄ is reducible, ρ̄ ≅ χ̄_1 ⊕ χ̄_2 with (χ̄_1/χ̄_2)|_{I_{ℚ_q}} = ϵ^{i−1} or ϵ^{1−i}. In general the projective image of ρ̄ contains an element whose order lies in {(q + 1)/gcd(q + 1, i + 1), (q + 1)/gcd(q + 1, i − 1), (q − 1)/gcd(q − 1, i − 1)}.
items.note: Added by the review REV-PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B. Stated as the paper uses it, with m = a(q − 1)b and ω_2^m = ι^{−1}χ|_{I_{ℚ_q}}. Split from item 34, whose layer (R24.3, prescribed global lifts) does not plan it. This local computation of residual inertia for tame potentially Barsotti–Tate types (Breuil–Kisin modules with descent data) is in the direction of FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.4 ('including descent data … Separate finite-flat, potentially Barsotti–Tate and merely potentially semistable cases') and R07.5 ('Local residual types'). Routed as a source of those layers.

routes.title: Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions, Part II: automorphy lifting for symmetric powers and the removal of supercuspidal primes
routes.brief: Build on Modularity, automorphy and Langlands endpoint extensions (ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions), whose ML.3 plans Newton–Thorne symmetric-power automorphy as an endpoint. This Part II owns the method of Newton–Thorne, 'Symmetric power functoriality for holomorphic modular forms, II' (Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), 117–152). That method removes the hypothesis of Newton–Thorne I that no local component is supercuspidal. It is a sibling of the Part IIs proposed for Newton–Thorne I (SymmetricPowersByAnalyticContinuation) and for Clozel–Thorne (SymmetricPowersByUnitaryLevelRaising). It takes their endpoint, Newton–Thorne I Theorem B (PAPER-NEWTON-THORNE-21-B item 42, planned in ML.3), as the case sc(π) = ∅. Final theorems, as the paper states them. Theorem 2.1: let F be totally real, p a prime, ι : ℚ̄_p → ℂ, n ≥ 1, and π a regular algebraic cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_2(𝔸_F) of weight 2, non-CM, with r_{π,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} not ordinary for every v | p, and PSL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) ⊂ Proj r̄_{π,ι}(G_F) ⊂ PGL_2(𝔽_{p^a}) up to conjugacy for some a ≥ 1 with p^a > max(5, 2n − 1). Suppose π′ is regular algebraic cuspidal with (1) weight 2 and non-CM, (2) r_{π′,ι}|_{G_{F_v}} not ordinary for v | p, (3) r̄_{π′,ι} ≅ r̄_{π,ι}, (4) for each v ∤ p, π_v a character twist of Steinberg iff π′_v is, and (5) Sym^{n−1}r_{π′,ι} automorphic. Then Sym^{n−1}r_{π,ι} is automorphic. Theorem 3.1 (Theorem A): for every non-CM regular algebraic cuspidal π of GL_2(𝔸_ℚ) and every n ≥ 1, Sym^{n−1}π exists. Propositions 3.9–3.11: making a representation seasoned, removing one supercuspidal prime, and the weight-2 case with 2, 3 ∉ sc(π). Layers. (1) The setting of §2 and the rings: the reductions (6)–(11) by soluble base change (imported, item 48); Kisin's local rings (imported, item 6); R_Q, R^□_Q and their p = 2 variants (imported, item 7); Lemma 2.2 and the morphism P → R, where P is imported from PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (item 8). (2) Taylor–Wiles data with α^{n−1}, α^{n−2}β, …, β^{n−1} distinct; P_Q with its inertial relations, using the unique decomposition of item 51; and the unitary Hecke modules with twisted Taylor–Wiles level (Lemma 2.4, Proposition 2.5, with Labesse's descent, item 49). The quaternionic side (Proposition 2.3) is imported from GL2ModularityLifting. (3) Patching: Lemma 2.7 (with item 53) and Proposition 2.6 for p > 2; Lemma 2.9 and Proposition 2.8, with the Ĝ_m^γ-actions of item 60, for p = 2. (4) The support argument (item 16). Regularity of P_∞ at the automorphic point comes from the vanishing of adjoint Selmer groups, imported from PolarizedAutomorphyLifting (item 17), with the commutative algebra of item 52. Labesse's base change (item 49) and soluble descent (item 48) then prove Theorem 2.1. (5) Killing ramification: Definition 3.2, Lemmas 3.3–3.5 (with the types of SmoothRepresentationsPartII, Hida control of item 57 and the non-ordinarity criterion of item 47), Definition 3.6 (seasoned), Proposition 3.7 (with Dickson, item 55, and Gee's Theorem 4.6.1, item 61), Lemma 3.8 (library), Propositions 3.9–3.11 and the reductions in the proof of Theorem 3.1 (with the large-image theorem, item 56, Chebotarev, item 54, and BLGGT14 Theorem 4.2.1, item 36). Corrections the layers must respect. E1: in the proof of Theorem 3.1 the 3-adic image statement is about r̄_{π′,ι}. E3: in the case 2 ∈ sc(π), after replacing 3 by 2, conclude by the weight-2, 2 ∉ sc case already proved, not by Proposition 3.11, because π″ may have 3 ∈ sc(π″). E2 and E4 are notational (Frob_w, ad⁰, Q_N, H_G, H_{G,∞}, F for F⁺). The published version says 'potentially crystalline' on p. 148 where arXiv v2 says 'potentially Barsotti–Tate'; in weight 2 these agree.
